Pragati Field Manual

"Is this move paid for, and is it paid for on every timeframe?"

How every engine works, how to read a chart in context, how to tell a probe from an acceptance, how to trade the tested trend system and invest with the grid, six real markets reconstructed, and drills to practise on. Each claim is tagged with how well it is known.

How to read the evidence tags

Pragati was built and audited in public, and many of its parts were tested on markets. Not all of them were. Every claim in this manual carries one of three tags.

MeasuredTested in this repository on real market data with a pre-registered plan, and on data the design never saw. The numbers are in docs/trail-lab.md and docs/trail-tradability.md.
ExternalMeasured in the v9 audit (380 instruments, six asset classes, three eras), whose data lives in a separate repository. The numbers are quoted in the script and were not re-checked here.
UnmeasuredA reading aid or a reasoned combination. Useful for context, never proven to make money. Size accordingly.
Part I

Foundations

Chapter 1

Getting started

1.1

Setup in five minutes

Add Pragati to the chart.

It opens in its own pane under price, and it draws the trail, the volume profile and the readout table on the price chart itself.

Use standard candles.

On Heikin Ashi, Renko, Kagi, Point & Figure or range bars the prices never traded, so every family pauses and says "non-standard chart".

Start on the daily chart.

Daily bars are what was tested. Weekly bars were tested for the ▲ and the grid. Intraday works, but nothing on it was measured.

Leave the defaults alone at first.

View Full, Trace Conviction × Value, conviction on Ladder down, value on Ladder up, Accepted momentum on. Every number in this manual was measured at these settings.

Give it history.

Conviction's histogram needs about 450 bars to calibrate (1.8 years of daily bars). Until then the push gate is warming: the grid's rows have no memory, the trail cannot start, and the readout says so.

Create one alert.

Choose the condition "Any alert() function call" on Pragati. It carries every event once, at its bar's close (section 31.1).

1.2

Reading a chart in sixty seconds

Five looks, in this order, at the close of a bar. The worked readings come from the readout in Figure 2.2.

Is there a reading?

Anything paused, warming, stale or gold means smaller or later. In Figure 2.2 nothing is gold.

Trader: the AUCTION row's CHART cell.

LONG 0.62: the tested system is long, at size 0.62. Size it with the formula in section 18.1.

Investor: the CVG row's STATE.

Buy 2.71: the TURNED family (buyers in control, price cheap). Weight it at 2.71 units in the book.

Why: the CVG row's WHY and PUSH.

"buyers running · turning up" and ↑: both edges are confirmed and a push is on. Nothing is held.

Context: OI and the auction.

"Long build-up · book 62 pct": new longs, the book not crowded. "Migrating ↑ · trail ↑ · in value": value is moving with the trail. A stop belongs below the trail or the session VAL.

Chapter 2

The visual language

2.1

The colour grammar: one hue, one job

Colours mean the same thing everywhere in Pragati. Learn these six and every element reads itself.

Green · direction up, action buyBuyers in control, a rich value reading, a long position, a Buy or Accumulate action.
Red · direction down, action sellSellers in control, a cheap value reading, a short position, a Trim or Exit action.
Gold · caution, never a directionRead with care: a probe, a quiet regime, a held row, a crowded book, short covering, crypto's capitulation.
Grey · neutralNothing to read, Hold or Wait, Accepted momentum flat.
Blue · the session profile's value areaIdentity, not direction. The VAH, VAL and value rows.
Slate · the trail's rolling value ribbonIdentity: a different value area from the session profile's.
On the value tape, green means rich and red means cheap. A red value tape is a price below fair value, which is what the capitulation ▲ wants.
2.2

The pane, labelled

A column's colour is not who is in control. Control is the trace's side of zero. A green column under a trace at −45 means sellers still control, with their grip easing. When the market is unusually quiet the columns lose half their colour: a loud pane in a quiet market is drawn quiet.

2.3

The price chart, labelled

Chapter 3

How Pragati thinks

3.1

The one question

After this chapter you can
  • say in one sentence what Pragati measures, and in one more what it does not claim

"Is this move paid for, and is it paid for on every timeframe?" Everything in Pragati is a way of asking that question, and each engine asks a different part of it:

Paid for in effort

Conviction: how much of the bars' travel became displacement, and how consistently, weighted by participation. A move that went far on little agreement is not paid for.

Paid for in price

Value: where price stands against a model of fair. A move that has already carried price rich is paid for in the other sense: it is late.

Paid for in acceptance

The auction: whether the market's value has followed price. A break that value has not followed is a probe.

On every timeframe

The ladder reads conviction from inside the bar and value from above it, so one chart answers on three horizons.

What it does not claim. Most of what Pragati draws describes. Measured without look-ahead, the pane's readings carry almost no timing information of their own External. Three things here carry measured leans:

  • the grid's capitulation state and the ▲ that marks its turn External;
  • the grid's graded units across a book External;
  • Accepted momentum, across many markets Measured.
The setup lab adds measured facts about breaks: what a probe does to a trend, and what gets accepted Measured. Everything else is structure for reading, tagged Unmeasured.

Design rules you will meet everywhere:

  • Gold means caution, never direction.
  • Nothing pauses silently.
  • Nothing that fires repaints.
  • Every claim carries its evidence.

3.2

The engines in plain words

Conviction

How much of the window's effort turned into net movement, weighted by participation (volume, or true range where there is none).

Answers: who is in control? · Seen in: the Conviction trace, the conviction tape, the histogram.

Value (Samanvaya)

Where price stands against fair value: a macro-hedged relative-value leg blended with a breadth leg, in σ. Past θ is cheap or rich.

Answers: is the price stretched? · Seen in: the value tape, the Value trace.

The ladder

Both readings across timeframes. Conviction on Ladder down reads the bars inside each chart bar. Value on Ladder up reads the chart and the frames above.

Answers: is it true on every timeframe? · Seen in: the two tapes.

The Conviction-Value Grid

The two tapes as a 3 × 3 map. Each cell is a family with an action and units, the weights Pragyam sizes from. External

Answers: what should a portfolio hold? · Seen in: the CVG row, the ▲▼, the tint.

The auction

A rolling volume profile of the chart's own bars: where participation was accepted, and whether value is migrating.

Answers: where has the market agreed on price? · Seen in: the trail, the ribbon, the AUCTION row.

Accepted momentum

The six-month acceptance trail sets the side; time-series momentum sets the size. Long only when both say up, short only when both say down. Measured

Answers: should a trend book be long, flat or short? · Seen in: the trail's colour, the AUCTION row's CHART cell.

Open interest

On futures: whether this bar's trading opened risk (builds) or closed it (covering, unwinding). External

Answers: what kind of positioning? · Seen in: the OI row, the gold cast.

Session volume profile

Where volume traded in the current session: POC, value area, VWAP, initial balance, naked POCs. Unmeasured

Answers: where are the reference levels? · Seen in: the right edge of the price chart.

Part II · how every engine works

The knowledge base

Chapter 4

The conviction engine

4.1

From a bar to a share

After this chapter you can
  • compute a bar's conviction and its participation weight by hand
  • say what the Agreement and Effort denominators measure, and why the default is Agreement
  • explain why participation is capped

Conviction is Pragati's first instrument and its oldest. It asks how much of a bar's travel became displacement, and how consistently bars resolve one way, weighted by how much participation stood behind them.

One bar

c = (close − previous close) ÷ true range bounded −1 … +1 w = min( volume ÷ EMA20(volume), 3 ) the participation weight

A bar that closes at its high after opening at the previous close has c = +1: every tick of its range became net movement. A bar that travels widely and closes where it started has c ≈ 0, however violent it was.

The weight w is the bar's volume against its own 20-bar average. Where a bar prints no volume, the last good print is carried through hollow bars. Where the symbol has no volume at all, as with index spot, relative true range stands in. That is the Auto setting of Participation. Volume, True range and Off force one choice. Off gives equal weights, a control: if the reading barely changes with it off, volume tells you nothing on that symbol.

The cap at 3 matters more than it looks. Expiry days, index rebalances and block prints carry volume many times normal. Uncapped, one such bar would own the whole window for its full length, and the oscillator would be reporting that one bar. The original author's tests found participation weighting earns its place, with Off the worst setting in all three signal architectures tested External.

The window: the raw share

Agreement (default) raw = 100 × Σ(c·w) ÷ Σ(|c|·w) over the Lookback (20 bars) Effort raw = 100 × Σ(c·w) ÷ Σ w

Agreement is Chande's form, the RSI family, applied to range-normalised closes weighted by participation. It asks how consistently bars resolve one way. A bar that went nowhere drops out of both sums, so heavy volume with no progress is invisible to it. Every number in the script's evidence was measured on this form.

Effort divides by total participation, which is Wyckoff's law taken literally. A heavy bar that went nowhere dilutes the reading, as Chaikin money flow divides by volume. It is untested Unmeasured. Whichever is chosen, the panel's effort → result row measures absorption under both (section 4.3).

Table 4.1 A worked raw share over four bars (constructed arithmetic)
BarClose changeTrue rangecVolume ÷ averagewc · w|c| · w
1+1220+0.601.21.2+0.720.72
2+315+0.200.80.8+0.160.16
3−816−0.502.02.0−1.001.00
4+1012+0.834.53.0 (capped)+2.502.50

Over these four bars Σ(c·w) = +2.38 and Σ(|c|·w) = 4.38, so Agreement reads 100 × 2.38 ÷ 4.38 = +54: buyers won most of the weighted travel. Effort divides by Σw = 7.0 and reads +34. Bar 3's heavy, failed sale counts against buyers in both. Bar 4's spike counts as 3, not 4.5.

4.2

Scaling, zones and the quiet regime

After this chapter you can
  • say what +30 and +60 mean on any instrument
  • explain why a dead market can read loud, and how Pragati marks it
conviction = 100 · tanh( raw ÷ 3σ ) σ = standard deviation of raw over the Normalization window (200)

The raw share is divided by three of its own standard deviations and squashed by tanh, so the reading is bounded at ±100 and calibrated to the instrument. The inner zone, ±30, is occupied about a third of the time. The outer zone, ±60, is occupied about 4% of the time: measured at 3.2% to 4.3% External.

Two consequences follow, and both are easy to forget.

  • Scaling is relative. +60 is extreme for this instrument over this window. It is not a universal overbought line. Past the outer zone is where trends run, and also where they end.
  • Scaled, not centred. Zero keeps meaning "neither side in control". On a persistently trending instrument one side's zone is simply visited more often.

The quiet regime

When σ itself collapses, a small imbalance divided by a small σ reads large. Pragati watches for this. The quiet regime is σ in the bottom fifth of its own history, ranked over four Normalization windows (800 bars at the defaults). While it holds:

  • the histogram's columns lose about half their colour, while the trace carries conviction;
  • the panel's raw-share row reads QUIET;
  • conviction's push gate shuts. The grid's rows hold, and the acceptance trail cannot step (section 8.2).

Quiet is not rare, and it clusters. On the repository's reference code it held on about a fifth of all bars, as designed, but on 85% of NIFTY 50's last 300 bars to October 2026 and 58% of gold's Measured. Chapter 25 shows what that does to the trail.

4.3

The histogram, its tiers and the push gate

After this chapter you can
  • read a column's hue, lightness and saturation as three separate answers
  • name the four tiers and say which ones open the push gate
  • say how long the gate takes to warm up

The trace is smoothed by a short EMA (Smoothing, 3) and compared with its own signal line (Signal EMA, 9). The histogram is the gap:

histogram = trace − EMA9(trace) impulse when |histogram| ≥ k · σ(histogram) k = 0.5, σ over 200 bars

A plain crossing of trace and signal is not a signal here. Two lines near zero cross endlessly, and k = 0 (a plain crossover) was the worst value out of sample in a 900-configuration search External.

Table 4.2 The histogram's four tiers
TierConditionDrawnPush gate
0 · impulseGrowing away from zero, past k·σNear-solidOpen, on its side
1 · buildingGrowing away from zero, below k·σModerateOpen, on its side
2 · deceleratingShrinking, the trace still moving with it (by more than 0.1σ of its bar-to-bar change)MidOpen, on its side
3 · turningShrinking with the trace flat or against itPaleShut

Hue is not control. A column's hue is which side of its signal line the trace is on, which is the direction of the push. A green column with the trace at −45 means sellers are still in control but their grip is easing.

The push gate

The gate is the one thing every layer of Pragati that "moves" waits for. The grid's rows move only on it (section 7.1), and the acceptance trail starts and steps only on it (section 8.2):

gate = +1 histogram ≥ 0, tier 0, 1 or 2, not quiet gate = −1 histogram < 0, tier 0, 1 or 2, not quiet gate = 0 tier 3 (turning), or the quiet regime

It always reads conviction's own histogram, whichever trace the pane draws. Only on the Conviction trace are the pane's columns the gate's columns.

Warm-up. The histogram's σ needs a clean 200-bar window of a histogram that itself needs the trace's 200-bar σ. The gate therefore reads from about 450 bars, 1.8 years of daily bars. Until then the grid's rows have no memory, the trail cannot start, and the readout says gate warming.

Effort → result

The panel's row Σ|c|·w ÷ Σw is the share of the window's participation that became directional displacement. At 100%, every bar closed at its extreme. In the bottom fifth of its own history the row turns gold and reads ABSORBED: effort met by opposing orders, which can resolve either way. Only the ◆ reads it; requiring absorption did not improve the ▲ External.

Chapter 5

The value engine

5.1

Samanvaya's two legs

After this chapter you can
  • say what 'cheap' and 'rich' mean in Pragati, and what they do not mean
  • name the two legs and what each one sees

Value is Samanvaya's engine, carried into Pragati line for line. Where conviction asks who is pushing, value asks where price stands against fair. Cheap and rich are statistical statements about this price against a model of it. They are not statements about a company's worth.

Leg 1 · Relative value (RV)

The chart's own return is hedged against a stepwise-selected basket of macro drivers (rates, currencies, commodities and the like). A custom ninth driver can be added. The residual spread is scored over an ensemble of timescales.

The hedge is applied in proportion to its measured skill, its rolling out-of-sample R² (Macro hedge · Auto). The model is fitted on an anchored clock: one observation per closed day by default, or per week. It spends 22 of Pine's 40 data requests.

Leg 2 · Breadth

Seven causal views of the chart's own price: the Market Strength Factor at five timescales, plus the fastest as momentum only and the slowest as flow only. It is the price-only half of Tattva's Swayam ensemble.

Breadth is momentum, so it overlaps conviction. The panel's layer overlap row measures by how much rather than assuming it away.

The two legs are blended in z-space, with their correlation measured, at Leg mix 0.5: the equal blend Samanvaya measured best (+0.0691 against +0.0637 for RV alone) External. Set the mix to 1.0 to see value without momentum.

On every timeframe

The model takes one observation per closed anchor period, a day by default, and each observation is the sum of the chart-bar returns inside it. Before the fix, on a 5-minute chart the whole macro fit ran on one closing 5-minute return a day, and value carried no macro information. The panel's value · macro share row shows how much of value is relative value on this chart.

Driver timing. On a daily NSE chart many drivers close hours later; TVC:US10Y closes about eleven hours after NSE. A driver whose bar closes more than a third of a bar late is read at its previous close, the value known at the chart's close. The panel's value · driver timing row shows what was lagged.

5.2

From z to θ: the value scale

After this chapter you can
  • convert θ into the pane's units
  • say when the value tape leaves grey
value = 100 · softbound( 0.5 · z ) z = Samanvaya's unified z (RV ⊕ breadth) θ = 1.5 (in |z|) → ±43 on the pane and the tapes

Value is positive when price is rich and negative when it is cheap. θ, θ · value threshold, is where Samanvaya calls price cheap or rich: 1.5σ at the default, which lands at ±43. The literature standard for a mean-reversion entry is 1.5 to 2.5. θ sets:

  • the grid's columns, and with them the ▲ (DOWN · cheap) and the ▼ (DOWN · rich);
  • the value tape's knee and the ◆'s and H's value tests;
  • the inner rail of the Value and blended traces.

Colours are flipped on purpose. On Pragati's value tape, green is rich and red is cheap, the reverse of Samanvaya's own pane. A rally makes price rich and conviction positive, so both tapes turn green together. A split in hue between them is then the thing the eye catches.

Warm-up. The value tape stays neutral grey until Samanvaya's model is built: ten anchor periods past a twelve-period hold-out, and the basket settled. While a basket settles after a rotation, a blended trace dims.

Measured. The 1.5σ entry and the leg mix are Samanvaya's own measurements on 24 targets External. The v9 audit varied θ from 1.0 to 2.0 and kept the capitulation edge at every value; none beat 1.5 in its worst era External.

Chapter 6

The ladder and the four tapes

6.1

The ladder of timeframes

After this chapter you can
  • list the frames each ladder reads on your chart
  • explain how a lower frame is read without sampling only its last bar, and a higher one without repainting
  • recognise a fallback (↺) and the intrabar depth limit

Both instruments are read across a fixed ladder of standard frames, the same on every venue. A frame is used only if the larger of the two holds a whole number of the smaller's bars; a reconstruction that split bars across bars would be inventing data.

Table 6.1 Which frames each ladder reads
ChartLadder down (conviction default)Ladder up (value default)
3m1m · 3m4h · 1h · 30m · 15m · 3m
5m1m · 5m4h · 1h · 30m · 15m · 5m
15m1m · 3m · 5m · 15m4h · 1h · 30m · 15m
30m1m · 3m · 5m · 15m · 30m4h · 1h · 30m
1h1m · 3m · 5m · 15m · 30m · 1h4h · 1h
4h1m … 1h · 4hnone → falls back ↺
D1m · 3m · 5m · 15m · 30m · 1h · 4h · DW · D
W1h · 4h · D · Wnone for conviction ↺; value M · W

Ladder down asks whether the chart's conviction is built from the horizons inside each bar. It is faster than chart conviction. Ladder up asks whether it is held by the horizons that contain the chart, and is slower. With the defaults (conviction down, value up) every reading spans three horizons: inside the bar, the chart, and above it.

The value ladder keeps Samanvaya's own rungs. Ladder up carries the whole composite on every higher frame. Ladder down reads only the three frames nearest below (daily reads 30m · 1h · 4h · D), breadth leg only: the RV leg cannot be re-run per rung inside Pine's request budget.

How a lower frame is read

Sampling a 1-minute rung at the daily close would describe the last few minutes of the day. Instead each lower frame runs the full engine on its own history, and the chart bar takes the participation-weighted average of that frame's reading across all its bars inside the chart bar: the bar seen from inside. TradingView caps the intrabars one request carries, about 100,000 on most plans, so the finest rungs reach back less far than the chart. Older bars run without them, and the panel's rungs live row says how many rungs a bar carried.

One disclosed drift. The depth cap counts back from today. As days pass, the oldest bars fall out of a fine rung's reach. After a reload, a ▲▼ at the left edge of that coverage can appear or vanish. A bar inside every rung's reach never changes.

How a higher frame is read

A higher frame read the usual way is a staircase, or it repaints. Pragati reconstructs it instead:

  • from the parent frame comes only its settled state as of its last closed bar;
  • from the chart comes the parent bar now forming, aggregated from the chart's own bars.
The result lands on the parent's settled value at its close and is identical in history and in realtime. The panel's ladder · rebuild error row reports how closely it landed, in points.

Fallback ↺. A direction with no frames on this chart reads the other direction instead of pausing every signal, and the tape's label shows ↺. That happens with Ladder up on 4h, 45m or monthly, and with Ladder down on 1m. Equal weight goes to every rung. The standard frames are not evenly spaced, so the tape leans toward wherever rungs are dense. That is the price of a familiar ladder, stated rather than hidden.

6.2

The four tapes and the amalgamated view

After this chapter you can
  • read all four tapes' hue and intensity without a legend
  • tell WIDENING from REVERTING, and RUNNING from PAUSING
  • read the amalgamated view's TALL tapes
conviction tape (+82) 100 · tanh( mean over the ladder of raw ÷ 3σ ) chart rung included value tape (−82) 100 · softbound( 0.5 · mean over the ladder of z ) momentum tapes (±89) Ladder down: tape − chart reading Ladder up: chart reading − tape

Each rung is fused in linear z-space and compressed once, so agreement across frames is rarer than any one frame's reading. A bright tape means the whole ladder is stretched, not one horizon.

Table 6.2 The four tapes
TapeHueIntensityWhat it answers
MTF conviction (+82)Green buyers, red sellersFaint inside ±30, a clear step brighter past it, solid past ±60Who controls across the ladder, and how far
MTF conviction momentum (+89)Which way the faster view pullsNear-solid while the pull grows past k·σ; moderate while it grows below; pale while it shrinksLadder down: BUILDING or TURNING INSIDE the bar. Ladder up: RUNNING AHEAD or a PULLBACK

Phases: how the grid reads the momentum tapes

Each momentum has a standing side that changes only past its own knee: k·σ for conviction momentum, 0.5σ for value momentum. Until a knee is calibrated, the side is the sign. That side, read against its level tape's edge, is the phase the grid's WHY cell prints:

Table 6.3 Confirmed and unconfirmed phases
InstrumentConfirmed phaseUnconfirmed phase
Conviction (rows)Running: momentum on the row's side. Buyers or sellers are pressingPausing: momentum against the row. A pullback inside the control
Value (columns)Reverting: momentum against the dislocation. Turning up from cheap, down from richWidening: momentum with it. Still cheapening, still richening

Note the opposite rules. Conviction's edge is confirmed by the same hue outside it; value's by the opposite. Inside the capitulation cell, value reverting beat widening in every era External. That is why the ▲ waits for it.

Amalgamated

Each momentum setting can read Separate band (default), Amalgamated or Off. Amalgamated draws the grid's fold for you. Past its edge, a level tape stands TALL while its momentum confirms the edge, and short while it does not. Inside its edge it stays short and faint.

Table 6.4 Amalgamated tapes
The tape looksIt meansGrid reading
Short, faintNo edgeFAINT row, or FAIR column
Short, brightAn edge, unconfirmedPausing, or widening
TALL, brightAn edge, confirmedRunning, or reverting

A bright red conviction tape over a TALL red value tape is the ▲'s condition, drawn: sellers in control, price cheap, the cheapening turning up. Amalgamated drops the bands' shading and the early TURNING INSIDE read, both unmeasured. Keep Separate if you use them. Switching a band off hides the band, never the reading.

Chapter 7

The grid engine and the signals

7.1

Rows, columns and the row memory

After this chapter you can
  • say exactly when the grid's row moves, and when it is HELD
  • explain why the column has no memory and the row does

The grid reads the two level tapes into a 3 × 3 map (chapter 11). It is readable only on a standard chart with both level tapes ready.

target row UP if conviction tape ≥ +30 DOWN if ≤ −30 FAINT between column RICH if value tape ≥ +43 (θ) CHEAP if ≤ −43 FAIR between

The column follows the value tape directly, every bar. The row has a memory. It moves to its target only on a push gate (section 4.3) toward it:

Target above the row, and the gate is +1

The row moves up to the target.

Target below the row, and the gate is −1

The row moves down to the target.

Anything else

The row stays where it is. If the target differs, the row is HELD, and WHY says so in gold.

No gate yet (warming)

The row simply equals its target, with no memory. WHY appends gate warming.

This is why a tape that slips briefly across ±30 does not flip a family. Pragyam's grid ignores a tape move that conviction's own histogram has not confirmed. A row move takes both the tape crossing and a push that way, on the same bar or later.

Held is caution, not direction. A held row means the tape has left the row and the histogram has not confirmed a push that way. The family's units stay between the held row and half-way to the neighbouring row, according to how firmly the push holding it is drawn.
7.2

The 5 × 5 and the graded units

After this chapter you can
  • compute a name's units from its position on the map
  • explain what PAUSING and WIDENING do to the units

Each of the nine families has units (chapter 11), but STATE rarely prints a cell's round number. The name is placed on the map at a position, and the units are read there, bilinearly between cells, as Pragyam does.

The position

How intensely each tape is drawn

A tape's ink runs from 0.12 to 0.45 inside its knee (±30 for conviction, θ for value), steps to 0.65 at the knee, and rises to 1.0 toward solid (±60 for conviction, ±70 for value). The row position is the row times conviction's ink; the column position is the column times value's ink.

Half-way for an unconfirmed edge

A row that is PAUSING, or a column that is WIDENING, is moved half-way toward the middle: the 5 × 5's in-between cells.

Held rows

A HELD row sits between itself and half-way to its neighbour, by how firmly the push is drawn.

Reading the units at a position

rows −1 … +1 (DOWN … UP), columns −1 … +1 (CHEAP … RICH) units = bilinear interpolation of the nine cells at (row position, column position)

Worked (constructed). Sellers in control, the conviction tape at about −45 and running: row position −0.8. Price cheap, the value tape at about −62 and reverting: column position −0.9. The four surrounding cells are DOWN·cheap 4, DOWN·fair 1.5, FAINT·cheap 1.5 and FAINT·fair 1.

along the column DOWN row: 0.9 × 4 + 0.1 × 1.5 = 3.75 FAINT row: 0.9 × 1.5 + 0.1 × 1 = 1.45 along the row 0.8 × 3.75 + 0.2 × 1.45 = 3.29 units

STATE prints Buy 3.29. If value momentum were still widening, the column position would halve to −0.45, and the same name would read 2.35 units. The tooltip shows the unshaded cell too; here, 4.00.

Measured. The units table is v8's, re-measured in v9 and kept. The graded units, read as a position, were positive in all three eras outside crypto External. Buy · capitulation went from 3 to 4 units in v9.1, because at 4 the grid improved or tied in all three eras on both scorers External.

7.3

The signals, exactly

After this chapter you can
  • state the ▲ and ▼ conditions completely
  • explain why a ▲ can come days after the grid entered the cell, or never
  • list what pauses each family, and how the pane tells you
Table 7.1 The signal families
SignalFires on the first closed bar whereAlso needsEvidence
▲ Capitulation turnthe grid stands in DOWN · cheap and value momentum is REVERTING, having not been so on the bar beforeA standard chart; both level tapes and conviction warmed up; the bar before readable; the long cooldown (10 bars) clearExternal +0.046 to +0.056σ over 10 bars, every era, daily; positive weekly
▼ Distributionthe grid enters DOWN · rich (sellers in control of a rich price)The same, with the short cooldownExternal As a state, underperformance in every era; too rare to measure as an event
◆ Continuation (off)conviction above zero; the histogram dipped below zero within 6 bars and now crosses +k·σ; conviction tape ≥ +30; value tape below +θ; effort not absorbedThe full stack, including the trace's warm-upExternal Negative in both eras outside crypto
R regular divergence (off)a price higher high on a conviction lower high (zone gate), the ladder also lower, value rich (> 0) at the pivotPivots 5 left and 5 right: the divergence is known 5 bars lateExternal About zero in every era

Entered means entered. A grid that becomes readable already inside a cell never entered it. Warm-up completing is not a capitulation, so a ▲▼ needs the bar before to be readable too. The ▲ fires on the first bar of the turn, not the first bar of the cell. A market can sit in DOWN · cheap, widening, for weeks with no ▲, and the ▲ comes only when the cheapening eases. It may never come.

The declaration is the last ▲ or ▼, standing until the opposite one, with no exit. Held as a position it carried no edge External. The state behind the ▲ did, which is why the pane background paints the state by default: green while the grid stands in DOWN · cheap, deeper once value momentum has turned, and red in DOWN · rich.

Crypto. The capitulation reading failed on crypto, which trends, so on a crypto symbol its tint and its ▲ are drawn in gold. Nothing that fires changes.

Nothing pauses silently. A tape that is warming or switched off, no frames after fallback, or Samanvaya's model still building pauses the families that read it. A gold SIGNALS PAUSED label at the pane's right edge names the layer. While only the trace is warming, the ▲▼ run and the label names just ◆, R and H.

Chapter 8

The auction engine and Accepted momentum

8.1

The rolling profile and migration

After this chapter you can
  • say which window the trail uses with Accepted momentum on and off
  • draw the five migration states from two value areas

The auction engine builds its own volume profile from the chart's bars. It does not read the session profile, whose settings and session change with the timeframe. Its window is 126 bars, six months, with Accepted momentum on (the default), and the conviction Lookback (20 bars) with it off. The ribbon, the probes, the AUCTION row and the trail all use that same window.

Weights

Each bar contributes its capped participation weight w (section 4.1), spread evenly from its low to its high. Raw volume let one expiry print own the POC for the whole window; flips were 2.0× likelier on the bar such a spike left the window, a flip caused by nothing.

An absolute grid

Bins are a power of two of the tick nearest ATR(20)/4, at most 300. A bin edge moves only when volatility changes by about √2, never because the window's low did. Anchored at the window's low, 29% of the value area's bin-sized moves had been phantom.

POC and value area

The POC is the heaviest bin; ties go to the bin nearest the middle. The value area starts at the POC and adds the heavier neighbour, above or below, until it holds 70%. VAL and VAH are its edges.

Migration: this window against the window N bars ago

Table 8.1 The five migration states
StateCondition (first match)Reads
+2 · Migrating ↑Today's VAL above the old VAHThe value areas no longer overlap. Value has moved up
+1 · Shifting ↑Today's POC above the old VAHThe centre of value has left the old value area
0 · BalanceAnything elseValue overlaps where it was
−1 · Shifting ↓Today's POC below the old VALThe mirror
−2 · Migrating ↓Today's VAH below the old VALThe mirror

With a 126-bar window the comparison is with the value area of six months ago: a slow, structural question. In a trend, migration usually reads ±1 or ±2 for months. NIFTY 50 read Shifting or Migrating ↑ on 189 of its last 300 bars, and Balance on only 21 Measured.

Measured (setup lab S5, section 16.2). With Accepted momentum agreeing, bars Migrating with the trail did better over 20 bars than bars in Balance, in all three sets. The result was consistent but not confirmed Measured.

8.2

The acceptance trail: start, step, probe, flip

After this chapter you can
  • apply the trail's four rules to a bar
  • explain why the default trail can sit far from price for months
  • read the trail's colour with Accepted momentum on and off

The trail is the ratcheted far edge of value: the value-area low while up, the high while down. It is the floor or ceiling of where the market has accepted price. It is updated on closed bars only and never repaints.

Table 8.2 The trail's rules, checked in this order
RuleWhile up (D = +1); down mirrorsEffect
StartMigration ≥ +1, push gate +1, close ≥ VALD = +1, level = VAL
FlipClose below the level, and the window's POC below it, and migration ≤ −1D = −1. The level is unchanged: the broken floor becomes the ceiling
ProbeClose below the level without both of the flip's other conditionsNothing changes; the bar is a probe. Its first bar is marked with a gold ×
StepMigration ≥ +1, push gate +1, VAL above the level, close ≥ VALLevel = VAL. A floor is never lifted above price

So the trail moves only when value shifts its way and conviction confirms a push that way: the same gate by which the grid moves a row. It flips only on acceptance, meaning price beyond it, the market's value (the POC) following, and value having migrated that way. Price beyond it without all three is a probe: in Market Profile terms, price outside value that has not been accepted.

Why the trail can sit far from price

A step needs the push gate open, and the quiet regime shuts it (section 4.2). In a long, orderly trend conviction's σ can sit in its bottom fifth for months, and the trail cannot step at all. On gold, the trail's floor stayed at 2,640 from before August 2025 to 27 May 2026 while price traded as high as 5,586. It stepped to 4,256 on 28 May, the first open gate with value migrated Measured. NIFTY 50's trail sat at 24,064 for the whole of its last 300 bars (chapter 25).

With Accepted momentum on, the trail's level is not a stop. What trades is the side (with momentum's size), not the distance to the line. A trail 30% below price is still long. For stops, use section 21.2.

Colour

Table 8.3 The trail's colour
Accepted momentumHueIntensityNeutral or gold
On (default)The sideThe size: solid at 0.5 and above, strong from 0.25, faint belowNeutral grey when flat: the trail and momentum disagree
OffThe sideThe conviction tape in the trail's direction: solid past ±60, strong past ±30, faint againstGold when the value tape is stretched past θ its way: the move is already paid for

The value ribbon is the rolling value area as a slate band with its POC dotted, over the last 1,500 closed bars. Inside the band is in value; above or below is price the window has not yet accepted. Probe marks keep the latest 40. A probe lasts about four bars, and marking every bar of it turned a quarter of the chart gold.

8.3

Accepted momentum, from the inside

After this chapter you can
  • compute S and the position from a chart's numbers
  • say what each word in the AUCTION row's CHART cell means
for h in 21, 63, 126, 252 bars: s_h = clip( ln(close ÷ close h bars ago) ÷ (σ·√h), −2, +2 ) S = mean(s_h) ÷ 2 in −1 … +1 (σ: EWMA of daily returns, span 60) position = side × max(0, side × S) side = the 126-bar trail's D weight = position × 10% ÷ annualised volatility, capped at 2

The side is where value was accepted over six months. The size is how far and how consistently price has gone over one, three, six and twelve months, each in its own volatility. Where the two definitions of trend agree, the position is the trail's side at momentum's size. Where they disagree, it is flat.

Table 8.4 The AUCTION row's CHART cell with Accepted momentum on
CHART cellMeaning
LONG 0.62Trail up, S = +0.62: long at size 0.62
SHORT 0.40Trail down, S = −0.40
FLAT · disagreeThe trail and S point opposite ways

The cell is live on the forming bar and final at the close. The tested system decides at the close, trades at the next open, and rebalances weekly with a 10% band (section 18.1). Its position alert, through the one Any alert() function call alert, fires on each change of LONG, SHORT or FLAT. It is off by default, because an alert invites trading one chart, and the tested edge is a portfolio's.

Chapter 9

The session profile and open interest

9.1

The session volume profile

After this chapter you can
  • say which session the profile covers on your timeframe
  • read POC, VAH, VAL, HVN, LVN, naked POCs, VWAP and IB, and know which are measured

The session profile is a price-chart overlay, display only: nothing in the engine reads it. It answers where volume traded in the current session.

Table 9.1 The profile's session
Chart timeframeSession
IntradayThe day
DailyThe week
WeeklyThe month
Monthly and aboveTwelve months

How it is built

  • From intrabars, by actual traded price, when Build from intrabar data is on and the plan delivers them. Otherwise each bar's volume is spread over its range. The panel's Profile Mode row reports which, and the session's intrabar share.
  • Volume or time. Volume is used when at least half of the last 500 bars print it. Otherwise the profile is time-at-price (TPO), automatically, and the session line reads TWAP instead of VWAP.
  • Bins are ATR(20) ÷ 4 wide (Bins per ATR), frozen at the session's start, or a fixed number of ticks. A bar wider than 200 bins is spread over its whole range on every st-th bin, with volume conserved.
  • POC: the first bin to reach the session's maximum. Value area: 70%, walked out from the POC, the larger neighbour first.
  • HVN / LVN: a local peak at least 1.2σ above the mean of the non-empty rows, or a local trough at or below their 10th percentile. These are heuristics; the thresholds are unmeasured.

Levels drawn

Table 9.2 Session profile levels
LevelWhat it isEvidence
POC, VAH, VALThe session's most-traded price and its 70% value areaUnmeasured
Developing trailsHow POC and value developed through the session; blank on its first barUnmeasured
Prior session valueLast session's pPOC, pVAH and pVAL, drawn only across the current sessionUnmeasured
Naked POCA prior session's POC price has not traded back through: at most 5, at most 250 bars old. Since v9.9 a session's POC joins the ledger before its first bar's touch check; before, 27% of drawn naked POCs had already been traded throughUnmeasured (PVOI's "measured" label not re-verified)
Session VWAP / TWAPThe session's volume-weighted average price; time-weighted without volumeUnmeasured
Initial BalanceThe high and low of the session's first 12 bars, intraday only: on daily bars 12 bars would swallow the weekUnmeasured
Delta splitEach row split into inferred buying and selling, by close location per bar or the tick rule per intrabar. An inference, not order flowUnmeasured

The panel's Location row places price: above, below or in value, or at the POC (within one bin). Off value is gold, because unaccepted price can resolve by rejection or by acceptance, and the colour does not pretend to know which.

9.2

The open-interest engine

After this chapter you can
  • explain how ΔOI becomes a σ figure and a character
  • recognise every feed state, and why an expiry is not conviction
  • say when the OI row should be believed

Volume answers how much traded. Open interest answers what kind: whether the trading created open risk or destroyed it. The sign of ΔOI is the information volume cannot carry.

The companion series

Built from the chart's prefix and ticker as PREFIX:TICKER_OI, then two alternates. It is never built from the tickerid, which on a modified chart is a JSON envelope. It is requested on the same timeframe, with no look-ahead.

Is it live?

At least a fifth of the last 50 bars must carry a change; otherwise the row reads STALE. An end-of-day OI series on a 5-minute chart is a step function.

The build figure

The bar's log change, divided by the RMS of the last 50 accepted changes, measured before this bar joins. RMS keeps zero at zero, so the sign is the sign of ΔOI. It needs 10 accepted changes first; until then the row reads WARMING.

Structural bars

A bar that moves more than half the book, or one beyond 3σ that also moves more than a fifth of it, is an EXPIRY / ROLLOVER. Such bars are kept out of the baseline, so one roll cannot inflate σ for the next fifty bars.

The character

Beyond ±0.5σ, the sign of ΔOI with the sign of the close's change: long build-up, short build-up, short covering, long unwinding. A book that moves while the close does not reads PRICE FLAT.

Trust

ρ(|ΔOI|, activity) over 50 bars must reach 0.20, or the row dims. Activity is volume, or true range without it. The signed correlation would be wrong by construction: OI rises on long and short builds alike.

Table 9.3 OI feed states
Feed stateMeaningColour
liveA readingBy character
warmingBuilding its baseline (10 changes)Gold
staleFewer than a fifth of recent bars changeGold
daily onlyOI exists on daily bars onlyGold
noneThe symbol has no open interest at all, as on cash equity and spotNeutral: the correct answer
no symbol / syntheticA malformed ticker, or a non-standard chartGold

Crowded: the book's level at or above the 80th percentile of its last 250 bars, which prints gold in WHY. The gold cast on the histogram, on by default, tints a column toward gold when exits paid for its push: covering outnumbering long build-ups above zero, or unwinding outnumbering short build-ups below, with at least a third of the window exits. It applies only with the feed live, outside structural bars, and trusted. Pushes it marks did worse than others in both eras on 240 NSE F&O stocks External.

The four-quadrant reading is a practitioner's framework. The academic evidence lives at a monthly horizon (Hong and Yogo 2012). Nothing validates the bar-level quadrant. "Self-limiting" is a hypothesis this table colours by, not a result Unmeasured. On a continuous front-month future the book falls into each expiry as positions roll, and a fall below the structural cut can read as covering or unwinding. Treat OI in expiry week with caution.

Budgets

Pine allows 40 unique data requests. Samanvaya spends 22; the ladders up to 10; the profile 1; OI 4. At most 37 execute on any chart, so nothing more can be requested. Part III

Reading every state

Chapter 11

The Conviction-Value Grid

Rows come from the conviction tape: UP past the inner zone (+30), DOWN past −30, FAINT between. Columns come from the value tape: CHEAP past −θ, RICH past +θ, FAIR between. Each of the nine cells is a family named for what it says to do. The number is its units, the relative weight a portfolio gives the name.

Rows move only on a push

A row changes only when conviction's own histogram confirms a push that way: on the move's side, not turning, not in a quiet regime. Without that push the row is held where it was, and WHY shows "held" in gold. This stops the grid flickering on every wobble of the tape.

The 5 × 5: phases

Each edge has a momentum that confirms it or not. Conviction confirms a row while buyers (or sellers) are running; it is pausing otherwise. Value confirms a cheap or rich column once it is turning back toward fair; it is still cheapening or still richening otherwise. An unconfirmed edge sits half-way to the middle, so its units fall. Inside a cell the units are also shaded by how strongly each tape is drawn.

Table 11.1 Phases in the WHY cell
You see in WHYIt meansEffect on units
buyers running · sellers runningConviction momentum stands on the row's sideThe full row
buyers pausing · sellers pausingA pullback against the rowHalf-way to the middle
turning up (from cheap) · turning down (from rich)Value momentum reverting toward fairThe full column. On DOWN · cheap this is the ▲'s condition
still cheapening · still richeningThe dislocation is still wideningHalf-way to the middle
no edgeFAINT and FAIR: nothing to confirmWait, 1 unit
· held (gold)The tape left the row without a push that wayBetween half and all of the held row, by the push's strength
· gate warmingConviction's histogram is still calibrating (about 450 bars)Rows follow the tape with no memory yet
Chapter 12

The readout table

Five columns ask the same question on every row. STATE: where the layer stands. WHY: what makes it so. PUSH: what pushes it now. CHART: one more reading that differs by row. SPAN: how long it has stood, counting the current bar as the first. Hover any cell on TradingView for its tooltip.

OI row (futures with open interest)

Table 12.1 OI row states
STATEColourWhat happened this bar
Long build-upGreenPrice up, open interest up: new longs, risk committed
Short build-upRedPrice down, open interest up: new shorts, risk committed
Short coveringGoldPrice up, open interest down: a rally paid for by exits. Short-covering rallies lagged External
Long unwindingGoldPrice down, open interest down: a decline paid for by exits
BalancedGreyThe change is within 0.5σ of zero
Price flatGreyThe book moved past 0.5σ but the close did not, so there is no side
Expiry / rollGoldOver 50% of the book in one bar, or over 3σ and 20%: structural, ignored
Warming Stale feed Daily only No symbol PausedGoldNot enough history yet, an end-of-day feed, no OI at this timeframe, a chart modifier, or a non-standard chart
No OIGreyThe instrument has no open interest. Correct for cash equity and spot

WHY adds who is doing it and how full the book is: "book 85 pct" means total open interest sits at the 85th percentile of its last 250 bars. From the 80th it turns gold: a crowded book. PUSH is the change in σ. A faded row means the size of the book's change does not track activity (ρ below 0.20), so do not read it. Expiry caution: a front-month future's book falls into every expiry as positions roll, which can read as covering or unwinding. Unmeasured

Part IV

Reading in context

Chapter 14

The context stack

14.1

The six layers, top down

After this chapter you can
  • read any chart in a fixed order, so no layer is skipped and none is read twice
  • say which layer can veto which

Every reading on Pragati belongs to one of six layers. Read them in this order. A higher layer sets the meaning of everything below it, and a layer that cannot be read stops the reading there.

1 · Readable?Standard chart, warmed up, nothing paused
→
2 · RegimeTrend, balance, transition, quiet, dislocation
→
3 · LocationIn value, out of value, against the trail
→
4 · Control and valueThe grid family and its phases
→
5 · FlowOpen interest, crowding, the gold cast
→
6 · Trigger▲ ▼, a flip, an AM change
Table 14.1 The context stack
LayerWhere to lookQuestionsIt can veto
1 · ReadableSIGNALS PAUSED label, grey tapes, gate warming, non-standard chart, the panel's rungs liveIs every layer I am about to read actually computed?Everything. A paused layer is not a neutral reading; it is no reading
2 · RegimeAUCTION STATE (migration), the trail's side, Accepted momentum's CHART cell, the panel's raw-share row (QUIET)Is value moving, and do the two definitions of trend agree?Trade entries: no trend trade in a FLAT · disagree regime
3 · LocationThe value ribbon, the trail, the session profile's Location rowIs price accepted here, or probing beyond?Chasing: a probe is a caution on the trend (section 16.2)
4 · Control and valueCVG STATE, WHY and PUSH; the pane's tapes and backgroundWho controls the ladder, is price cheap or rich, and are both edges confirmed?Adding: no adds into a held row or a widening dislocation
5 · FlowOI STATE and WHY; gold-cast columnsIs risk being opened or closed, and is the book crowded?Size, never direction
6 · Trigger▲ ▼ on the pane; the AUCTION row's CHART changes; alertsHas a measured event happened at this close?—

Why this order. Readability first, because a paused layer looks like a neutral one. Regime before location, because "below value" means a probe in a trend and a rotation in balance. Location before the grid, because the grid knows nothing about where value was accepted. Flow is a size modifier and never sets direction: the four-quadrant reading is unmeasured at the bar level Unmeasured. The trigger comes last, because a trigger read before its context is a coin flip with a story attached.

14.2

The five-minute top-down routine

After this chapter you can
  • run one routine on every chart, at every close you act on
  • write the reading down in one line
Weekly chart, one minute

Grid family and phases (the ▲ and the grid were tested weekly). Trail side. Is the weekly value tape solid either way? This is the tide.

Daily chart: readability

Any gold label, grey tape or gate warming? Note it, and read only what is computed.

Daily chart: regime

AUCTION STATE and the CHART cell. Write trend up, trend down, balance, transition (FLAT · disagree) or quiet.

Daily chart: location

Close in value, above or below the ribbon? Any probe × in the last five bars? How far is the trail, in ATRs?

Daily chart: control and value

CVG STATE with units; WHY phases; PUSH. Is anything HELD?

Daily chart: flow

Futures only: OI character and crowding. Stale, warming or untrusted means skip this layer.

Daily chart: trigger

A ▲ or ▼ at this close? Did the CHART cell change? Did the trail flip?

Write one line

For example: RELIANCE · D · readable · trend down (SHORT 0.50) · below value, no probe · Accumulate 1.5, sellers running, still cheapening · no OI · no trigger.

The line takes ten seconds once the routine is habit, and it is what your journal stores (section 21.4). Two weeks of lines on the same market teach more than any chapter here.

14.3

Timeframes without double counting

After this chapter you can
  • choose a decision timeframe and an execution timeframe
  • avoid reading the same horizon twice

Pragati already reads several timeframes inside one chart: conviction from inside the bar, value from above it (section 6.1). Opening a second chart one step up does not add a fresh opinion. A daily chart's value tape is the weekly and the daily. Use other timeframes for different jobs, not for more votes.

Table 14.2 Timeframe jobs
JobTimeframeWhyEvidence
Investing decisionsWeekly, then dailyThe ▲ and the grid were measured on both; weekly is calmerExternal
Accepted momentumDaily, decided at the closeThe only timeframe it was tested onMeasured
ExecutionIntraday (15m to 1h)To choose an entry inside the next session: never to change the daily decisionUnmeasured
Swing contextDaily trail and ribbonValue over six monthsUnmeasured
Intraday trading5m to 1hNothing was measured, and costs eat most measured edges below dailyCosts: External

When weekly and daily disagree. The weekly grid in DOWN · cheap while the daily reads UP · cheap means a turn is starting inside a weekly dislocation. That is the picture the capitulation plan is built for, and the daily leads. A weekly Exit · distribution with a daily Buy is a bounce inside distribution: the daily does not overrule the weekly for a holding.

Chapter 15

Regimes, and how meaning changes

15.1

Five regimes and how to tell them apart

After this chapter you can
  • name the regime from the readout in under a minute
  • know what each regime does to every other reading
Table 15.1 The five regimes
RegimeHow it readsWhat it changes
TrendTrail side and S agree: LONG 0.45 or SHORT 0.38. AUCTION STATE Shifting or Migrating its way, for weeksBreakouts from value in its direction did better than pullbacks into it (section 16.4). Probes against it are cautions on the trend, not reversals
BalanceAUCTION STATE Balance; S small; price rotating inside the ribbon; the trail flat or recently flippedEdges of value are references, but no setup is measured here Unmeasured. The grid's FAINT families dominate
TransitionFLAT · disagree: the trail and momentum point opposite ways. Often follows a flip, or a long probe clusterAccepted momentum is flat by design: no trend trade. On the 126-bar trail, a probe with migration already toward it flipped 15–28% of the time within 20 bars, against about 4% otherwise Measured
QuietPanel raw-share row QUIET; desaturated columns; the push gate shut; the trail frozen far from priceReadings are amplified: a small imbalance reads large. The grid's rows hold. Do not read the trail's distance as risk Measured
DislocationThe value tape solid past θ; the grid in a CHEAP or RICH family; pane tinted green (capitulation) or red (distribution)The investor's regime. Capitulation followed by gains in every era outside crypto; distribution by underperformance External

Regimes overlap. A market can be in a trend and quiet at once, which is the common case for an orderly index, or in a dislocation inside a downtrend. Write both. The regime that changes your action is the one to lead with.

Part V · measured

Fakeouts and traps

Chapter 16

Probes and acceptance

16.1

The life of a break

After this chapter you can
  • follow a break from its first bar to its resolution
  • say how often each outcome happens, on both trails

A break is a close beyond the trail. It is resolved in one of two ways. Either the market's value follows and has migrated, and the break is accepted, so the trail flips at that close. Or it does not, and the bar is a probe: a gold × marks its first bar. A probe then either flips the trail later or ends with price back on the trail's side.

Probe onset ×A close beyond the trail; POC or migration not with it
→
Probe episodeA median of 4 bars on the 126-bar trail, 3 on the 20-bar
→
RejectedBack on the trail's side, no flip
→
or acceptedPOC beyond and value migrated: the trail flips
Table 16.1 What breaks become (DEV · HB · HA, setup lab)
126-bar trail (default)20-bar trail (AM off)
Probe onsets measured6,012 · 3,019 · 31,96111,955 · 5,706 · 62,616
Back on the trail's side within 5 bars57% · 58% · 57%56% · 56% · 55%
Flipped within 10 bars2.3% · 1.9% · 1.9%27% · 28% · 26%
Flipped within 20 bars4.5% · 3.8% · 4.2%59% · 59% · 59%
Median probe length4 bars3 bars

The two trails behave like different instruments. A six-month floor is almost never broken by a probe: fewer than one probe in twenty is followed by a flip within a month. A twenty-bar trail flips after most probes, and at about the rate the same rules produce on driftless random walks (58%). On the short trail, a probe says little beyond the trail's own mechanics Measured.

16.2

What a probe does to the trend

After this chapter you can
  • say what the gold × is worth, measured
  • stop treating probes as fakeouts to fade

The prediction, written before the test, was that probes are fakeouts: after one, the trail's side should do at least as well as it usually does. It came out the other way, in every set and on both trails Measured.

Table 16.2 After a probe onset (setup lab F1)
Outcome on the trail's side, beyond its average barDEV (2006–19)HB (2020–26)HA (411 unseen markets)
126-bar trail, next 10 bars−0.076σ (t −3.0)−0.048σ (t −1.9)−0.070σ (t −8.5)
126-bar trail, next 20 bars−0.092σ (t −2.2)−0.038σ (t −1.4)−0.080σ (t −8.7)
20-bar trail, next 10 bars−0.056σ (t −3.4)−0.039σ (t −2.3)−0.048σ (t −8.2)
The probe is a caution on the trend, not a fakeout. On the default trail it almost never flips the side, but the side's next two to four weeks are weaker than usual, by about 0.05 to 0.09σ. That is exactly what gold means in Pragati: smaller, or later. Do not add on a probe. Do not fade it either (next section). Hold, and let the trail decide.

The sizes are small, as every honest edge here is: a lean measured across thousands of events, worth acting on only as a size adjustment across many markets.

16.3

What gets accepted: the fakeout checklist

After this chapter you can
  • score a break against four conditions at the close
  • know which conditions matter on which trail

Four features of the break bar were tested, each predicted in advance to make acceptance likelier. A break that will be accepted is the opposite of a fakeout.

Table 16.3 The four conditions (setup lab F2; DEV, HB and HA all reported in docs/setup-lab.md)
At the probe's first bar20-bar trail: flips within 20 barsVerdict126-bar trailVerdict
Depth: the close at least 0.5 ATR beyond the trail71% vs 54% (HA; t 37.5)Confirmed Measured4.3% vs 4.1%Not supported
Weight: participation w ≥ 1.562% vs 57% (HA; t 9.7)Confirmed Measured3.2% vs 4.5% (fewer)Not supported (opposite)
Push: the push gate against the trail60% vs 55% (HA; t 8.6)Consistent Measured3.4% vs 4.8% (fewer)Not supported (opposite)
Migration already toward the break62% vs 58% (HA; t 5.1)Consistent Measured15–28% vs about 4%Consistent Measured
Table 16.4 Flip rate within 20 bars by the number of conditions met
Conditions met01234
20-bar trail, HA (62,616 probes)51%56%62%71%72%
20-bar trail, DEV52%57%64%73%77%
20-bar trail, HB49%57%63%69%66%

The checklist

  • Which trail? On the 126-bar default, only migration matters: is AUCTION STATE already Shifting or Migrating toward the break? If not, the break is very unlikely to be accepted within a month.
  • On the 20-bar trail, count: depth ≥ 0.5 ATR · participation ≥ 1.5 · push against the trail · migration toward the break.
  • Zero or one condition: about one break in two is accepted, the rate of chance. Two or more: about two in three. Three or more: about seven in ten.
  • Whatever the count: a probe on the 126-bar trail is a caution on the side you hold (section 16.2).

On the six-month trail, hard and heavy breaks were less likely to flip it. A six-month floor is not broken by one day's force; it is broken when value moves.

16.4

Entries around value, measured

After this chapter you can
  • say which of four entry rules carried timing beyond the trend itself

Four entries were tested on the 126-bar trail. Each was measured against the trend's own average bar, so a positive number is timing beyond simply being on the right side.

Table 16.5 Four entries (σ beyond the trend's average bar; setup lab S1–S4)
Entry at the close10 bars: DEV · HB · HA20 bars: DEV · HB · HAVerdict
Rejection: the first bar back on the trail's side after a probe−0.03 · +0.02 · −0.04 (t −5.3)−0.06 · +0.05 · −0.04Not supported Measured
Acceptance: the flip bar, in the new direction+0.02 · +0.09 · +0.08 (t 4.4)+0.05 · +0.11 · +0.11 (t 6.7)Consistent Measured
Pullback into value, AM agreeing−0.00 · +0.01 · −0.00−0.01 · −0.05 · −0.01Not supported Measured
Breakout from value, AM agreeing+0.06 (t 4.1) · +0.05 (t 2.5) · +0.06 (t 10.4)+0.04 · +0.04 · +0.05Positive everywhere; not predicted Measured
With the trend, the break of value beats the return to it. A close out of value in the trend's direction, with Accepted momentum agreeing, did better than the trend's average bar in all three sets. A pullback into value did not, and the difference between the two was significant everywhere (t −2.5 to −11.5). Buying the dip into value is the intuitive trade, and it measured nothing here. Breakouts were not predicted, so treat the result as strong evidence that a fresh test must still confirm.

Hit rates sit between 50% and 54%. None of these is a setup that wins most of the time. They change when you act inside a trend that Accepted momentum already holds, and by how much.

17.2

The fakeout protocol

After this chapter you can
  • run a five-question check before acting on any break
Is this bar closed?

If not, nothing has happened yet.

Which trail, and which event?

A flip is acceptance. A gold × is a probe. A close out of the ribbon with the trail is a break of value, not of the trail.

If it is a probe against my position

Do not exit on it, and do not add. On the 126-bar trail it is a caution: if you trade discretionarily, size down by a step, or wait (section 16.2).

If it is a probe in my favour (against the trail)

Do not enter on it. Score it (section 16.3). On the 126-bar trail, only migration toward it makes acceptance plausible.

If it is a break of value with the trend

The measured better entry. Is Accepted momentum agreeing (LONG or SHORT, not FLAT)? Then it is the moment to act if you were waiting to (section 20.3).

Part VI · systematic and swing

Trade guide

Chapter 18

Accepted momentum

18.1

The tested system

This is the one trade system in Pragati that passed a held-out test Measured. It was chosen by a fixed rule from eleven trials on data up to 2019, frozen, and then run once on 2020-26 and on 411 markets it had never seen.

Table 18.1 Accepted momentum, the tested rules
RuleExactly
SideThe acceptance trail on a 126-bar (six-month) window: up while value has migrated and ratcheted up, down while it has migrated down
Momentum score SThe 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month moves of the close (21, 63, 126, 252 bars), each divided by volatility × √horizon, capped at ±2, averaged and halved, so S lies between −1 and +1
PositionSide × max(0, side × S): LONG with size S when both say up, SHORT with size |S| when both say down, FLAT when they disagree
Decide and tradeRead at the close; trade at the next open. Never on the forming bar
SizeWeight = size × 10% ÷ annualised volatility, capped at 2 (two times the market's capital slice)
VolatilityThe test used an exponential average (span 60) of daily log returns, × √252. On TradingView the built-in Historical Volatility indicator with length 60 is a close stand-in Unmeasured
RebalanceOnce a week (every fifth bar in the test). Each market moves to its target only if the target has moved by more than a tenth of itself. That includes going flat and changing sides: between rebalances the position is left alone
When an alert arrives. The position alert fires on the close where the side changes. Under the tested rules you act at the next weekly rebalance. Acting at the next open instead is faster, but that variant was not tested.

Worked sizing example

Book ₹10,00,000 across 20 markets → slice per market ₹50,000 Stock X: readout says LONG 0.62; annualised volatility 28% weight = 0.62 × 10% ÷ 28% = 0.221 notional = 0.221 × ₹50,000 = ₹11,071 price ₹2,500 → buy 4 shares (₹10,000), the nearest whole lot Cap: weight never above 2.0 (notional ₹1,00,000 for this slice)
18.2

Running it as a portfolio

Table 18.2 Results on held-out data
HoldoutSharpe, net of costsTiming beyond leaning longWorst drawdownMarkets positive
411 unseen markets+0.79 (t 4.0)t 4.1−3.7%79%
119 markets, 2020-26+1.21 (t 3.7)t 2.2−2.5%80%
  • The edge is a portfolio's. On one market the median Sharpe was only +0.23 to +0.38, and about a quarter of markets lost money over the period. Run the same rules on many markets at once.
  • It did not beat plain momentum by the pre-registered test. It matched it at lower turnover and drawdown.
  • Costs. At twice the assumed costs the Sharpe was still +0.69 and +1.11.
  • Risk level, and real drawdowns. At 10% per market the diversified book ran at only about 1.3% to 1.6% volatility, which is why its drawdowns above look small. Scaled to 10% volatility for the whole book, the same paths would have drawn down roughly 16% to 29%. Expect drawdowns of that size at a useful risk level. Getting there needs futures-style leverage, and shorting Indian cash stocks overnight needs stock or index futures.
  • How many markets. The tested books held 119 and 411 markets. With fewer, results drift toward the single-market figures. About 20 to 30 markets across several classes is a practical floor Unmeasured.
  • Where it was weak. The INR currency pairs lost; crypto was about flat (section 27.4).

The costs the test charged

Table 18.3 Costs charged in the test
ClassIndex futures and ETFsFXCommoditiesUS stocksNSE stocksCrypto
One way, per change in weight5 bps3 bps8 bps10 bps15 bps20 bps
Before capital: six months of paper trading at the same costs, then one-tenth of the intended size for six months. Stop if the drawdown exceeds 1.5 times the backtest's worst, or if the rolling 12-month Sharpe stays below zero for two quarters.
Chapter 19

Initiating and positioning

19.1

From the close to the order

After this chapter you can
  • run the tested system's daily timeline without improvising
  • handle a gap, a missed open, a holiday and a partial fill

The tested system decides at the close of bar t and holds from the open of t+1 to the open of t+2. Every result in chapter 18 was computed that way. The timeline below keeps you inside it.

Table 19.1 The tested timeline
WhenWhatNotes
At the closeRead the AUCTION row's CHART cell on every market in the bookA forming bar is not a decision (section 10.1)
After the closeCompute each target weight (section 19.2). Is today a rebalance day?The test rebalanced weekly, every fifth bar; pick a fixed weekday and keep it
After the closeOn a rebalance day, change only the markets whose target moved more than 10% of itself. That includes flips and going flatBetween rebalance days the position is left alone, flips included
Next openPlace the orders at or near the openThe test traded the open. A market-on-open order is the closest match

When reality does not match the test

Table 19.2 Departures from the timeline
SituationDo thisWhy
The market gaps at the openExecute anywayThe test's returns are open to open: gaps are already in its numbers
You miss the openExecute at the next price you can, the same day; do not wait for a better oneWaiting for a better price is a new, untested rule
A holiday on one marketTrade it at its next openEach market keeps its own calendar
A partial fill, or a lot larger than the targetRound down to whole lots; leave a remainder flatRounding up adds risk the sizing did not ask for
Crypto, which never closesUse the exchange's daily bar (UTC) as the closeThat is how the test's crypto bars were built
The weight is below one lotSkip the market, or use a smaller contractA slice too small to trade is common with large lots
19.2

Sizing, with real numbers

After this chapter you can
  • turn a CHART cell into a weight, a notional and a number of lots
  • say how much risk the tested sizing actually takes
weight = size × 10% ÷ annualised volatility, capped at ±2 (size = the CHART cell's number, with its side) notional = weight × the capital slice for that market (slice = capital ÷ number of markets) lots = notional ÷ (price × lot size), rounded down

Volatility is the EWMA (span 60) of daily returns, annualised by √252. On TradingView, the built-in Historical Volatility indicator with length 60 is a close stand-in. The 10% is a per-market volatility target at full size. Because size is usually well below 1, most positions run far below it.

Real numbers, 30 October 2026. The six case-study markets, read from the reference engine at that close, on ₹10,00,000 split into six slices of ₹1,66,667 Measured:

Table 19.3 A six-market book on 30 October 2026
MarketCHART cellVolatility (annual)Target weightTarget notional
NIFTY 50SHORT 0.2012.9%−0.158−₹26,366
RELIANCESHORT 0.5022.1%−0.225−₹37,460
Gold (USD)FLAT · disagree22.0%0₹0
USD/INRLONG 0.108.6%+0.117₹19,576
BTC/USDTFLAT · disagree27.9%0₹0
BANKBEESSHORT 0.1613.2%−0.123−₹20,559

The gross exposure is about ₹1,03,962, roughly 10% of capital, with two of six markets flat. That is typical. The tested book's volatility at 10% per market was only about 1.3% to 1.6% a year, because sizes are small and markets diversify one another Measured. Scaled up to 10% for the whole book, the same paths would have drawn down roughly 16% to 29%. Decide which you are running before you start.

Lots

With NIFTY at 23,053, a single index-futures lot is worth several times a ₹1.67 lakh slice (check the exchange's current lot size). Small accounts cannot hold index futures at the tested size. Use the ETF (NIFTYBEES), fewer and larger slices, or accept that the book holds fewer markets. Fewer markets means more single-market noise (section 18.2). Every rounding should go down, never up.

19.3

Scaling in, adding and taking off

After this chapter you can
  • know which scaling the system already does for you
  • add or reduce discretionarily without breaking the tested rules

Accepted momentum already scales. Its size is momentum's score, so as a trend strengthens over weeks the weekly rebalance adds, and as it weakens the rebalance takes off. Pyramiding and partial exits are built in. On the tested system, do nothing beyond the rebalance.

Discretionary traders who want to time inside the system's position, entering it or adding to it, have one measured tool and one measured caution Measured:

Table 19.4 Discretion inside the system
MomentActionEvidence
The CHART cell turns LONG or SHORTTake the first part of the position at the next openThe system's own decision Measured
A close out of value in the trend's direction, AM agreeingTake the next partBreakouts from value beat the trend's average bar Measured
A pullback into valueDo not add because of itNo edge measured Measured
A probe against the position (126-bar trail)Do not add; optionally take a step offThe side did worse than usual afterwards Measured
The next weekly rebalanceBring the whole position to the tested targetEnds the discretion: you are back on the system
Never average down against the system. Adding to a long that Accepted momentum has taken flat or short is a new strategy with no test behind it. The only measured buy-the-dip in Pragati is the investor's capitulation plan (section 23.1), which lives on the grid and at a different horizon.
19.4

Portfolio heat and correlation

After this chapter you can
  • cap correlated exposure
  • set a drawdown ladder before the first trade

The tested portfolio gave every market equal risk. In a real account, markets come in clusters that move together: Indian banks, oil and gas, precious metals, INR pairs. Ten bank stocks are not ten markets.

Count clusters, not tickers

Group markets that move together. Sizing treats each cluster as at most two or three slices in total, however many names it holds Unmeasured.

Cap gross exposure

Set a ceiling on the sum of |weight| across the book, for example 1.5× capital, so that low-volatility markets at their cap of 2 cannot dominate Unmeasured.

Write the drawdown ladder now

At the backtest's worst drawdown, halve all weights. At 1.5× it, stop and review: the system's kill rule (section 21.3).

Shorts need instruments

Shorting Indian cash stocks overnight needs futures. Without them, run long and flat only, and expect a different return profile from the test.

Part VII · weeks to months

Investment guide

Chapter 22

Investing with the grid

22.1

The investor's frame

For investing, the grid is the tool. Each name in your universe sits in one family, and its units say how much weight it deserves relative to the others. You hold everything you would hold anyway, more of what is cheap with sellers exhausted, and less of what is rich with sellers in control. Units are relative weights for a book of many names, not a buy-or-sell switch for one.

Evidence External: the graded units were positive in all three eras outside crypto. In Pragyam's allocator the units beat its seed weights in both eras on the Nifty 50 and the Dow 30.
Daily chartConviction on Ladder down, value on Ladder up: exactly what Pragyam sizes from.
→
Read at the week's last closeOne reading per name: the CVG row's STATE. Unmeasured cadence
→
Units to weightsWeight = units ÷ sum of units across the book.
→
Rebalance with a bandTrade only where a weight moved by more than a tenth of its target. Unmeasured house rule

Chapter 23

The investing setups

23.1

I1 · The capitulation plan

The one event the v9 audit found positive in every era is the capitulation turn. This is a staged plan around it. The staging itself is a house rule Unmeasured; the state and the turn are External.

1 · Enter DOWN · cheapThe green tint appears; STATE reads Buy 4. Buy the first third.
→
2 · ▲ firesValue momentum turns back toward fair; the tint deepens. Buy the second third.
→
3 · Leaves the cellBASING or FADING (Accumulate 1.5), or TURNED (Buy 3). Buy the last third on the next push ↑.
→
4 · BUILDINGHold 1.5. Let the position run.
→
5 · PAID or STALLINGTrim 0.75.
→
6 · ▼ DISTRIBUTIONExit toward 0.25.

When the plan is wrong

  • Crypto. The capitulation reading failed there. The tint and the ▲ are drawn gold. Skip the plan.
  • Gold readings. A held row, a quiet regime, "basket settling", or a paused grid. Wait for them to clear before adding.
  • A trend against you. If Accepted momentum is SHORT, the long-horizon trend still points down. Keep each tranche small (section 27.1).
23.2

I2 · The trend filter

I2Accepted momentum as an investor's filterMeasured not confirmed: drawdown halved, return halved
Context
A long-only book of stocks, ETFs or indices
Rule
Hold a name while its CHART cell reads LONG; hold cash (or the rest of the book) while it reads FLAT or SHORT
Check
Weekly, at the close, and immediately when the state changes; trade the next open
Size
Unlevered: the name's ordinary weight, or its grid units (section 24.1)
Evidence
Below. Max drawdown smaller in all three sets; Sharpe about equal except 2020–26, where buy-and-hold's was 0.23 higher. Invested 43–53% of the time
Fails when
Long, strong bull markets (it sits out the recoveries' first legs); the cost is about half the compound return
Table 23.1 The filter against buy-and-hold (setup lab I1; equal-weight, daily-rebalanced portfolios)
SetMarketsInvestedFilter: CAGR · max DD · SharpeBuy-and-hold: CAGR · max DD · Sharpe
DEV, 1992–201910646%11.5% · −31% · 0.8220.0% · −58% · 0.79
HB, 2020–2610653%7.4% · −29% · 0.8118.2% · −36% · 1.04
HA, 391 NSE stocks, 1997–202639143%16.5% · −28% · 1.3637.8% · −64% · 1.39
Read it as insurance, priced. The filter roughly halves the deepest drawdown and roughly halves the return. It is a choice about which pain you can sit through. It is not a better portfolio. HA is today's NSE listings, so it carries survivorship; only the comparison on the same markets is meaningful. The 20-bar trail made the same trade, −35% against −73.5% drawdown at 13.5% against 24.4% growth (section 24.2).

I3 · Staging and averaging

I3Entering in stagesUnmeasured a house rule
Context
Any name you intend to hold; the grid reads
Rule
Divide the intended weight into thirds. Each third needs a different, closed-bar reason
First third
The grid enters a Buy or Accumulate family (DISLOCATED, TURNED, BASING, FADING)
Second third
The ▲ (in DOWN · cheap), or the trend filter turning LONG, or a push ↑ that moves the row
Last third
The family improves (for example BASING to TURNED), or a weekly close confirms it
Averaging down
Allowed only inside the capitulation plan, and only while the grid stays in a Buy family. Never because the price is lower
Evidence
The families' units and the ▲ External; the thirds themselves are a house rule
Fails when
On crypto; in a held row; when a family is reached from above (TURNED falling to BASING is weakening, not a new entry)

I4 · Trimming and exiting

I4Trim and exit disciplineExternal states measured; the trims are units
Trim
PAID or STALLING: bring the name toward 0.75 units' share of the book
Exit
DISTRIBUTION (▼ marks its entry): toward 0.25 units, a token weight
Hold
BUILDING and IDLE change nothing. Do not add in BUILDING: buyers at a fair price lagged in v8
Speed
Trims are gradual: at each weekly review, move half the gap to the target Unmeasured
Evidence
Distribution was followed by underperformance in every era; the graded units positive in all three eras outside crypto
Fails when
A trim is read as a short; taxes and costs are ignored. Small trims in a large book are often cheaper skipped
23.5

I5 · The rebalancing calendar

After this chapter you can
  • run the investor's week in twenty minutes
Friday's close (or the week's last close)

Read every name's CVG STATE, units and WHY. Note ▲▼ and tint changes during the week.

Compute weights

Weight = units ÷ the sum of units, capped at about a tenth of the book per name (section 24.1).

Move half the gap

For each name, trade half the difference between current and target weight Unmeasured. Skip trades smaller than your cost threshold.

Apply the trend filter, if you use it

Names whose CHART cell is not LONG go to cash, or keep only their capitulation tranches (section 23.2).

Monday's open

Execute.

Monthly

Review the drawdown ladder, the clusters and the watchlist.

23.6

I6 · Building a watchlist

After this chapter you can
  • turn one indicator into a scan across many names

Pragati reads one chart at a time; it has no screener. A watchlist routine makes it scale.

Choose a universe and keep it

An index's members or a fixed list of ETFs. Changing the list because of recent winners is survivorship you add yourself.

One alert per name

Create Pragati's Any alert() function call alert on each chart with Alert on capitulation state entry / exit on. Every ▲▼ and every capitulation entry and exit arrives with the ticker, the grid's action and units, and both tapes.

A weekly sweep

Open each name on the weekly chart once a week and log its one-line reading (section 14.2).

Rank by units

Highest units first. That is the order the grid would allocate in.

Note the clusters

Five capitulations in one sector are one bet.

24.1

Building the book: a worked example

Six names, read at the week's close. Weights are units divided by their sum.

With a small book, one name can grow large. A practical cap of about a tenth of the book per name keeps the plan diversified Unmeasured. The more names, the closer you get to how the units were measured.

24.2

Investor risk

  • Trend filters trade return for drawdown. On 119 markets, holding only while the 20-bar trail was up cut the worst drawdown from −73.5% to −35%, but gave up about 11 points of yearly growth (13.5% against 24.4%) Measured. The 200-day average and plain momentum made the same trade. Accepted momentum used the same way, as a long-only filter, halved the drawdown in all three sets of the setup lab at about half the return (section 23.2) Measured.
  • The ▲ is a lean. About +0.05σ over 10 to 20 bars. It pays across many names and many events, not on any one External.
  • Gold is caution. Reduce or wait; never read gold as a direction.

25.1

How the cases were chosen

After this chapter you can
