These six cases are real daily bars, run through the repository's reference implementation of the auction engine, the push gate and Accepted momentum. The reference is the same code as the setup lab, and it was parity-tested against the Pine. They are not TradingView screenshots, and they show only what the reference computes:

They do not show the tapes, the grid or the ▲▼, which need TradingView's intrabar data and Samanvaya's macro drivers. Chapter 26's walkthroughs, which are constructed, cover those.

Table 25.1 The selection rule
RuleFixed in advance (docs/setup-lab.md §5)
MarketsOne per class: NIFTY 50 (index), RELIANCE (NSE stock), gold (commodity), USD/INR (FX), BTC/USDT (crypto), BANKBEES (ETF)
WindowThe last 300 daily bars to the data's end, 30 October 2026 (31 October for BTC, which trades daily)
EventsThe most recent event of each type before 30 September 2026 with a complete 20-bar outcome, whatever the outcome
CampaignsEvery campaign of the traded weight inside the window, winners and losers

So the cases were not picked for looking good. Several lose. The plates draw the trail as Pragati does with Accepted momentum on: hue is the side, intensity the size, grey when flat. Below each plate is the weight the tested sizing would have held. Letters mark the dates the text discusses. Event outcomes are in σ units, as in the setup lab: the move over 10 and 20 bars from the next open, in the event's direction.

25.2

NIFTY 50: a floor that never moved

A · 29 August 2025. The trail flips up at 24,064, with the close at 24,427. Value had shifted up (migration +1), and the window's POC, 24,864, stood above the old ceiling: acceptance. Momentum's S was −0.01, so the CHART cell read FLAT · disagree on the flip itself. The long campaign began only at the 3 September rebalance, once S turned up.

The floor never stepped. NIFTY rallied to a closing high of 26,329 on 2 January 2026, and the trail stayed at 24,064 throughout. Conviction's quiet regime held on 85% of these 300 bars, the push gate was shut, and a trail can step only through an open gate (section 8.2). The position did not care. With Accepted momentum on, the side and S decide, and the traded weight reached 0.65 during the rally.

B · 5 January 2026. The latest pullback into value before the cut-off, a setup-lab S3 event. NIFTY closed back inside value at 26,250, and over the next 10 bars it fell 2.67σ further. The pullback was not a buy, as the setup lab found on average (section 16.4).

C · 9 March 2026. The first of seven probes below the floor. Within 20 bars NIFTY traded down to 22,183, 8% below the trail, and still did not flip. Migration stayed +1 (value six months earlier was lower still), so the break was never accepted. S had turned to −0.33, so the system was already FLAT. That is the trail working as designed: acceptance is about value, not distance.

D · 19 June 2026. The flip down came with price almost on the line: close 24,013 against the trail's 24,064. The POC (23,968) had moved below and migration read −1. The level did not move; the broken floor became the ceiling.

E · 29 July 2026. The latest of five probes above the new ceiling, at 24,250. It was not accepted, and the market drifted (−0.28σ over 10 bars in the trail's direction). The short campaign began at the 18 August rebalance and was still open at the data's end, having made +0.55% on the slice while NIFTY fell 4.9%.

25.3

RELIANCE: right side, wrong timing

A · 20 August 2025. The trail flips up at 1,292.8 (close 1,406.5), and the CHART cell turns LONG 0.11. Yet the traded weight that day was still −0.09, from the earlier short. The traded position waits for the next weekly rebalance. That is the tested rule, and it is why the plate's weight strip lags the trail's colour.

B · 20 October 2025. The fourth step since early September, to 1,356.8. RELIANCE's gate was open far more often than NIFTY's (quiet on only 13% of these bars), so its trail ratcheted up behind the move.

The long campaign lost. It ran 65 bars from 21 October 2025 to 22 January 2026, and its size peaked as price did: the stock's closing high was 1,585 on 2 January. Net, it made −1.41% on the slice, while the stock moved −6.4% open to open. Momentum is strongest at the top of a move. That is the cost every trend system pays, and the reason the edge is measured on hundreds of markets.

C · 2 March 2026. The first of six probes below the floor (close 1,351.75 against 1,356.8), with migration 0. The probes came and went for four months without acceptance.

D · 16 July 2026. Acceptance: a close of 1,296.6, the POC at 1,302.4 below the trail and migration −1. The short campaign began at the 20 July rebalance.

E · 30 July 2026. A pullback into value on the short side (close 1,292.9). It did nothing measurable: −0.43σ against the trade over 10 bars, +0.14σ over 20. By 30 October the stock was at 1,165, below the value area. The open short campaign had made +0.56% on the slice while the stock fell 11.4%.

25.4

Gold: the size leaves before the line

The best campaign of the six. Gold's long ran 147 bars, from the window's start on 25 August 2025 to 25 March 2026. The weight reached 0.60, and the campaign made +14.5% on the slice while gold rose 32.9% open to open.

A · 2 March 2026. Gold closed at 5,294, near its closing high of 5,318 on 29 January, with S at +0.56. Over the next 20 bars it traded down to 4,101.

B · 25 March 2026. S had fallen to +0.09, and the weight with it, to 0.05. The campaign ended by size, not by the trail, which was then at 2,640: 42% below price. A stop at the trail would have given back almost everything. The system did not wait for it.

C · 28 May 2026. The trail finally stepped, from 2,640 to 4,256, the first bar in months with the gate open and value migrated. It stepped twice more within days, to 4,304.

D · 28 September 2026. The latest probe, at 4,168, below the floor of 4,304. It was not accepted within 20 bars; gold drifted to 4,038 (−0.41σ over 20 bars against the trail's side, as the setup lab's F1 expects). At the data's end gold closed at 3,899, 9% below a trail that still reads up. The POC was 4,440 and migration 0, so the market had not accepted the lower prices. S was −0.32, so the system was flat.

25.5

USD/INR: a staircase, and a quiet market's large weight

A textbook managed trend. In 300 bars there were no probes and no flips, and sixteen steps. The trail ratcheted from 85.12 to 91.68 as USD/INR climbed from 86.3 to 95.2. Migration read Shifting or Migrating ↑ on 267 of the 300 bars.

A · 31 October 2025. The first step, 85.12 to 86.00. B · 14 April 2026. A step to 88.64. C · 30 June 2026. A step to 90.88.

The weight. Annualised volatility was only 4.6% at the window's start, so even modest sizes asked for large weights. The weight reached 1.78, close to the cap of 2. One campaign held the whole window and was still open. Yet it made only +2.1% on the slice against a +10% move. The weight happened to be high on the days the rupee strengthened and low on the days it weakened. In the first quarter of 2026 the pair rose 3.0% and the position made almost nothing. A trend the trail followed perfectly still did not pay much.

D · 29 July 2026. The latest pullback into value, at 95.60: +0.01σ over 10 bars, +0.14σ over 20. Nothing to see, as on average.

25.6

BTC/USDT: a falling ceiling and a transition

A · 7 January 2026. The trail flips down at 106,240 (close 91,364): the POC at 88,000 had dropped below the old floor and migration read −1. Crypto trades every day, so these 300 bars span only ten months.

A ceiling that stepped. Crypto's push gate was open far more often (quiet on 14% of these bars), and the trail stepped down fifteen times, from 106,240 to 75,200, as BTC fell to a closing low of 58,625 on 30 June. B · 2 April 2026: one of those bars, with S at −0.48 and the trail stepping to 89,600.

Two short campaigns, both profitable but small. From 7 January to 16 April (100 bars) the system made +1.04% on the slice while BTC fell 15.6%. From 7 May to 19 August (105 bars) it made +0.17% on a fall of 8.7%. BTC's volatility (about 28% to 29% a year on this measure) kept the weight at 0.17 or below. High-volatility markets carry small weights by design.

C · 5 May 2026. A probe above the ceiling at 80,906. S had turned +0.07, so the cell read FLAT. The probe was not accepted, and the ceiling stepped lower again within weeks.

D · 21 August 2026. The latest probe above the ceiling (78,338 against 75,200), with S at +0.35. The trail is down and momentum up: FLAT · disagree, the transition regime (section 15.1). It was not accepted within 20 bars, and at the data's end BTC still sat above a down-trail in Balance, flat.

25.7

BANKBEES: a crash that was never accepted

A · 29 October 2025. After a long freeze, the gate opened with value migrated, and the trail jumped from 494.4 to 561.6 in one step. A trail that cannot step for months moves all at once when it can.

The long campaign ran from the window's start to 6 March 2026 (158 bars), with the weight up to 0.89. It made +0.22% on the slice for a +0.5% move.

B · 12 March 2026. A probe below the floor of 572.8. Within 20 bars the ETF fell to 516, 10% below the trail, and the break was still not accepted: migration stayed +1. It recovered to 591 by 21 April.

C · 21 April 2026. A step to 588.8. D · 8 July 2026. The flip down at 588.8, with the close at 587.7 and the POC at 561.6 below. Again the flip came with price at the line, not 10% beyond it.

E · 29 July 2026. The latest probe above the new ceiling (591.7). It was not accepted, and S was near zero, so the system stayed flat. By 30 October the ETF closed at 565.5, just below the value area's low edge, SHORT 0.16.

25.8

The six as one book

After this chapter you can
  • see what the tested edge looks like on six markets rather than four hundred

Run as one book, with equal slices from 6 January 2026 (the common start of the six windows) to 30 October 2026, net of the test's costs, the six markets made −0.69%. The worst drawdown was −1.29%, at an annualised volatility of 1.6% Measured.

Table 25.14 Six markets, 6 January to 30 October 2026
MarketContribution on its slice
NIFTY 50−1.72%
RELIANCE−3.10%
Gold+1.76%
USD/INR+0.12%
BTC/USDT+1.17%
BANKBEES−2.71%

That is a losing ten months, and it was chosen by rule, not for effect. It is also what the evidence predicts for a book this small:

  • on one market the median Sharpe was +0.23 to +0.38, and a quarter of markets lost over the whole test;
  • the edge appeared across 119 and 411 markets, sized alike;
  • the book's volatility, 1.6%, is the tested book's own (1.3% to 1.6%), which is why its losses are small too.
A trader who scales the book to 10% volatility should expect this kind of stretch to look six times larger.

Migrating ↓Value has left downward. A close below with the POC following flips the trail downValue moving with the trail. Steps are likely

Add the WHY cell. A probe is a break without acceptance. On the default 126-bar trail fewer than one in twenty is followed by a flip within 20 bars, yet the trail's side then does worse than usual for 10 to 20 bars (section 16.2) Measured. "Accepted, flips at the close" means all three conditions hold on the live bar.

Chapter 28

Conflicts and the decision tree

28.1

When readings disagree

Data first.

Non-standard chart, warming, paused, stale or gold: there is no reading. Do nothing new.

The horizon chooses the tool.

A trading book follows Accepted momentum. An investment book follows the grid's units. Do not let one book borrow the other's signal.

Gold reduces size; it never sets direction.

Held rows, probes, quiet regimes, crowded books and short covering all mean the same thing: smaller, or later.

Do not trade the untested parts.

The 20-bar trail, the ◆, R and H measured null or negative as signals. Read them as structure.

Crypto is the exception.

Skip the capitulation plan there.

28.2

The decision tree

After this chapter you can
  • go from a chart to an action through a fixed sequence of questions
Is the bar closed, and is every layer I need readable?

No → do nothing yet. Yes → continue.

Am I acting as a trader or as an investor?

Trader → 3. Investor → 7.

Trader: what does the CHART cell say?

LONG or SHORT → 4. FLAT · disagree → hold no position in this market; done.

Is today the rebalance day?

Yes → move to the target if it changed by more than 10% (section 19.1); done. No → 5.

Discretionary only: was there a break of value with the trend at this close?

Yes → optionally take the next part, within the target (T2). No → 6.

A probe against my position?

Yes → hold; optionally a step off (T4). Never exit on it alone, never add on it.

Investor: which family, and is anything gold?

Gold (held, quiet, settling, crypto capitulation) → wait. Otherwise → 8.

Is it a Buy or Accumulate family?

Yes → stage in by thirds (I3); add the second third on the ▲ in DOWN · cheap (I1). No → 9.

PAID, STALLING or DISTRIBUTION?

Trim toward 0.75, or exit toward 0.25 (I4). Otherwise hold, and rebalance on the calendar (I5).

Chapter 30

Answers and checklists

30.1

Answers

1DISLOCATED (DOWN · cheap), Buy · capitulation. Sellers running confirms the row; turning up is value REVERTING, the ▲'s condition. If value turned at this close, the ▲ prints on it. The deeper tint says the same. The unshaded cell holds 4.00. No: inside the capitulation cell the push's direction made no consistent difference, so a Buy there does not wait for a push ↑ (section 7.3).

2The conviction tape has fallen below +30, but conviction's histogram has not confirmed a push down, so the UP row is HELD (section 7.1). The units sit between Hold and half-way to the FAINT row. The investor makes no adds and no changes. Held is caution, not direction.

3Transition. The trail is up, momentum's S is not, and the system is flat. A probe below an up-trail is a caution on the long side: on the default trail, the side did worse than usual for 10–20 bars after probes (section 16.2). No long trade.

4T2, the break of value with the trend (section 20.3). The system is short, and the close has left value in the trend's direction. The system trades on its rebalance; a discretionary trader may take the next part within the target.

5Price is up while open interest falls: shorts are closing. Colouring it as self-limiting is a hypothesis {U}; pushes paid for by exits lagged other pushes in the v9 audit {X}. It changes size, never direction: a step smaller, or later.

6Nothing. The feed is live, but it has fewer than ten accepted changes for its baseline. Skip the layer (section 9.2).

7The ▲▼ (they need both level tapes) and the ◆, R and H. The grid is not readable while a level tape is not ready (section 10.2).

8DISTRIBUTION (DOWN · rich). Both edges are unconfirmed, sellers pausing and value still richening, so the position sits half-way toward the middle and the units are above the cell's 0.25. The investor exits toward a token weight; the ▼ marked the entry (section 23.4).

9A dislocation inside a downtrend: Matrix A's TURNED × AM SHORT, the classic conflict between horizons (section 27.1). The trader stays short by the system's rules. The investor builds in stages, with small tranches.

10No. The quiet regime shuts the push gate, so the trail cannot step and its distance means nothing. The side and S carry the position. Stops come from structure (section 21.2), and the book's risk from the drawdown ladder (section 19.4).

11No. The daily trader decides at the daily close. On a 15-minute chart the 126-bar trail and S's horizons are measured in 15-minute bars: a different and untested engine (section 14.3).

12No. The capitulation reading failed on crypto, which is why its tint and ▲ are drawn gold (section 15.3).

13Three of four conditions: depth ≥ 0.5 ATR, weight ≥ 1.5, and the push against the trail; migration toward the break is missing. On the 20-bar trail, breaks meeting three conditions were accepted about 70% of the time within 20 bars, against about 50% with none (section 16.3).

14On the 126-bar trail only migration toward the break mattered, and here it is Balance. Fewer than one probe in twenty was accepted within 20 bars. Hard, heavy breaks were if anything less likely to flip it. Expect no flip, and treat the probe as a caution on longs.

15Neither exit nor add. The system does not exit on a probe; a discretionary trader may take one step off (T4). After probes the trail's side did 0.05 to 0.09σ worse than usual over 10–20 bars (section 16.2).

16No. The rejection entry, the first bar back after a probe, measured nothing and was negative in HA (section 16.4).

17A break of value with the trend, the setup lab's S4: +0.06σ over 10 bars beyond the trend's average bar in all three sets, though it was not predicted. A discretionary trader may take the next part of the position, within the target (section 20.3).

18No. A pullback into value carried no edge beyond the trend's average bar, and breakouts beat it everywhere (section 16.4).

190.50 × 10% ÷ 25% = 0.20. Notional = 0.20 × ₹2,00,000 = ₹40,000 long.

200.30 × 10% ÷ 6% = 0.50, short: −0.50 × ₹2,00,000 = −₹1,00,000. Low volatility gives large weights.

210.90 × 10% ÷ 3.5% = 2.57, capped at 2.

22The sum is 10.5, so the weights are 38.1%, 28.6%, 14.3%, 9.5%, 7.1% and 2.4%. A per-name cap of about a tenth would redistribute the first two (section 24.1).

23No. In the tested system every change waits for the weekly rebalance, flips included (section 19.1).

24No. The change is 0.03, which is 7% of the new target, inside the 10% band.

30.2

Checklists

Every close (trader)

  • Bar closed; every layer readable
  • CHART cell on every market in the book
  • Rebalance day? Targets that moved more than 10%
  • Probes against positions noted; no exits on them
  • Breaks of value with the trend noted (T2)
  • Journal line written

Every week (investor)

  • Weekly chart read first for each name
  • CVG STATE, units and WHY at the week's close
  • ▲▼ and tint changes since last week
  • Weights = units ÷ sum, capped; move half the gap
  • Trend filter applied, if used (I2)
  • Clusters counted

Before any trade

  • Which setup card? (name it)
  • Context holds (regime, location)
  • Size from the formula, rounded down
  • Invalidation written
  • Not a trap from chapter 17

Before going live

  • Six months of paper trading at the test's costs
  • Markets chosen and fixed; clusters capped
  • Drawdown ladder and kill rule written down
  • Book volatility target chosen (the tested 1.3–1.6%, or scaled)
  • Start at a tenth of the intended size

Quick reference card

Every close

  • Gold anywhere? Smaller, or later.
  • Trader: read the AUCTION row's CHART cell; act at the next open.
  • Investor: read the CVG row's STATE at the week's last close.

Investor

  • Weight = units ÷ total units.
  • Stage into DOWN · cheap; add on the ▲.
  • Trim in PAID and STALLING; exit in DISTRIBUTION.
  • Not on crypto.

Trader

  • LONG or SHORT only when trail and momentum agree.
  • Weight = size × 10% ÷ volatility, cap 2.
  • Many markets, weekly rebalance.
  • Paper first, then a tenth.

Breaks

  • A probe is a caution on the trend, not a fakeout to fade.
  • 126-bar trail: only migration toward a break makes acceptance likely.
  • 20-bar trail: depth ≥ 0.5 ATR and weight ≥ 1.5 raise acceptance.
  • With the trend, act on the break of value, not the pullback into it.

Setups

  • T1 Accepted momentum is the only system.
  • T2 break of value: within the target.
  • T4 probe against you: hold, never add.
  • I2 trend filter: about half the drawdown, half the return.

Never

  • Trade the forming bar.
  • Read gold as a direction.
  • Lean on the ◆, R, H or the 20-bar trail.
  • Use non-standard candles.

Glossary

TermMeaning
AcceptanceA close beyond the trail with the window's POC beyond it and value migrated that way. Only acceptance flips the trail
Build-up · covering · unwindingOpen interest rising with the price move (new positions), or falling (positions closing)
CampaignA run of the traded weight on one side, from the rebalance that opens it to the one that closes it
CapitulationSellers in control across the ladder at a price cheap past θ: the DOWN · cheap cell
ConvictionThe share of the window's participation-weighted effort that became net movement
FamilyOne of the grid's nine cells, named for its action
FlipThe trail changing side on acceptance: a close beyond it, the POC beyond it, and value migrated that way
HeldA grid row kept in place because no push confirmed the tape's move
HVN · LVNHigh- and low-volume nodes: local peaks and troughs in the session profile
IBH · IBLThe initial balance: the high and low of the session's first bars (12 by default), intraday only
ImpulseA histogram column past k standard deviations of its history (↑↑)
Kill ruleStop the book if its drawdown passes 1.5 times the backtest's worst, or its rolling 12-month Sharpe stays below zero for two quarters
Ladder down / upReading the timeframes below the chart (inside each bar) or above it
MigrationThis window's value area against the one six months earlier: Migrating (no overlap), Shifting (only the POC left), Balance
Naked POCA prior session's POC that price has not traded back through
PhaseA momentum's standing side against its level tape's edge: running or pausing for conviction, reverting or widening for value
POC · VAH · VALThe most-traded price; the top and bottom of the 70% value area
ProbeA close beyond the trail without acceptance
Probe onsetA probe's first bar, the one marked with a gold ×
Push gateConviction's histogram on the move's side, not turning, not quiet
Quiet regimeRaw volatility in the bottom fifth of its history: readings are magnified
Rebalance bandThe tested rule: on a rebalance day a market's weight changes only if its target moved more than 10% of itself
SAccepted momentum's score, −1 to +1, from the 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month moves
Setup cardThe fixed form every setup in this book takes: context, trigger, entry, size, stop, exit, evidence and failure
SharpeReturn per unit of volatility, yearly. t is how far from zero it is, in standard errors
SliceA market's share of capital in an equal-risk book: the capital divided by the number of markets
Structural barAn OI change of more than half the book, or beyond 3σ and over a fifth of it: an expiry or roll, kept out of the statistics
θ (theta)Samanvaya's value threshold, ±43 on the pane at the default 1.5
TransitionThe regime in which the trail and momentum disagree, so Accepted momentum reads FLAT · disagree
UnitsThe relative weight a family gives a name in a portfolio
VWAP · TWAPThe session's volume-weighted average price; time-weighted when the symbol has no usable volume

This manual is educational. It describes how an indicator works and how it was tested; it is not investment advice. Past results, including held-out tests, do not guarantee future results. Trade only what you can afford to lose, and paper-trade first.
